product.facts: Scary Spider SEO is a free desktop site crawler and SEO auditor for Windows, macOS and Linux. It crawls a site (configurable depth, page limit, concurrency, optional robots.txt compliance, sitemap.xml seeding) and flags issues inline in a sortable table, with a plain-language explanation and fix for each. Checks include: 4xx/5xx and broken links/images, links to non-200 pages, missing/duplicate/too long/too short titles (30-60 chars, pixel width), missing/duplicate meta descriptions (70-155 chars), H1 issues, missing/duplicate H2, non-sequential headings, duplicate and near-duplicate content, low word count (<200 words), low text/HTML ratio, missing alt text, large images (>100 KB), images missing width/height, canonical problems (missing, multiple, to broken/redirect/non-indexable page), noindex/nofollow directives incl. X-Robots-Tag, long redirect chains, internal redirects, meta refresh, orphan pages (in sitemap but not internally linked), deep pages (depth >3), non-indexable or non-200 URLs in sitemap, indexable URLs missing from sitemap, non-descriptive or empty anchor text, pages with only one inlink, slow response (>600 ms), large HTML, missing OG/Twitter tags, missing viewport, mobile usability issues, JavaScript changing title/canonical/meta robots, content or links added only by JavaScript (optional headless Chrome rendering), invalid or missing structured data, accessibility violations (axe-core on rendered pages), insecure links, mixed content, missing HSTS/CSP and other security headers, missing lang, hreflang errors, uppercase in URLs. Exports to CSV. Never claim features not on this list, never claim pricing beyond 'free', never compare with named competitors.

existing.title: 5 Steps to Humanize AI Content & Save SEO

existing.title: Offpage SEO With Social Group Strategies That Work

posts.working_title: Technical SEO Audit: A Practical Checklist for Small Sites
posts.angle: The hub for the technical cluster. A prioritized, step-by-step audit a site owner can run in an afternoon: crawlability, indexability, status codes, redirects, sitemaps, duplicates, speed, mobile, HTTPS. Each step is short and links to the deep-dive post where one exists. Explains how to prioritize fixes by impact.
posts.avoid: Do not go deep on any single topic; link to the spoke instead.

posts.working_title: Robots.txt Explained: What to Block and What to Leave Alone
posts.angle: How robots.txt works, syntax (user-agent, disallow, allow, sitemap line), safe examples for common CMS setups, the classic mistakes (blocking CSS/JS, leaving a staging 'Disallow: /' in place after launch), and that disallow does not remove a page from the index. How to test it.
posts.avoid: Noindex vs disallow comparison is a later post; mention briefly only.

posts.working_title: XML Sitemaps: How to Build One Google Actually Uses
posts.angle: What belongs in a sitemap (only canonical, indexable, 200 URLs), what does not, lastmod honesty, size limits, sitemap index files, submitting in Search Console, and auditing a sitemap against a crawl (non-200 URLs in sitemap, indexable pages missing from it, orphan pages).

posts.working_title: How to Find and Fix Broken Links Before They Cost You Traffic
posts.angle: Internal vs outbound broken links, why they matter (crawl paths, user trust, lost link equity), how to find them with a crawl and in Search Console, and a fix decision tree: update the link, restore the page, or 301 to the closest equivalent. Custom 404 pages.
posts.avoid: Broken link BUILDING (outreach) is a later post; only mention it in passing.

posts.working_title: 301 vs 302 Redirects (and How to Fix Redirect Chains)
posts.angle: Permanent vs temporary redirects with a comparison table, when to use each (308/307 briefly), redirect chains and loops, internal links that point at redirects, meta refresh, and a cleanup process after a site migration.

posts.working_title: Why Google Isn't Indexing Your Pages (and How to Fix It)
posts.angle: Hub for indexing. Crawl vs index vs rank. Walk through the Search Console page indexing report statuses and the likely cause of each, then the fix. Covers blocked by robots, noindex, canonical elsewhere, duplicates, thin content, orphaned pages, and quality. Links to each spoke.

posts.working_title: Canonical Tags Explained: Fix Duplicate URLs the Right Way
posts.angle: What rel=canonical does (a strong hint, not a directive), self-referencing canonicals, common URL duplicates (parameters, http/https, trailing slash, www), canonical mistakes (pointing to redirects, 404s, noindexed pages, multiple canonicals, JavaScript changing it), and how to audit them.

posts.working_title: Noindex vs Disallow: Which One Keeps a Page Out of Google?
posts.angle: Comparison table, why combining disallow + noindex backfires (Google cannot see the noindex), meta robots vs X-Robots-Tag header for PDFs, which pages to noindex (thank-you pages, internal search, staging), and how to remove a page fast.

posts.working_title: Duplicate Content and SEO: What Actually Hurts and How to Fix It
posts.angle: Myth vs reality (no generic duplicate content penalty, but it splits signals and wastes crawling). Types: exact and near duplicates, duplicate titles/meta descriptions, boilerplate-heavy thin pages, product variants. Fixes: consolidate, canonicalize, rewrite, noindex.
posts.avoid: Do not re-explain canonical tags in depth; link to post 7.

posts.working_title: Orphan Pages and Internal Linking: A Simple Plan That Works
posts.angle: What orphan pages are and how to find them (sitemap vs crawl), click depth, pages with only one inlink, hub and spoke (topic cluster) linking, descriptive anchor text vs 'click here', and a repeatable process to add links when publishing new posts.

posts.working_title: On-Page SEO Checklist: 12 Things to Check Before You Publish
posts.angle: Hub for on-page. A pre-publish checklist: search intent, title tag, meta description, URL slug, single H1 and heading structure, intro, internal links, images and alt text, structured data, content depth, E-E-A-T signals, freshness. Each item links to its spoke where one exists.

posts.working_title: How to Write Title Tags That Rank and Get Clicked
posts.angle: Why titles matter, length in characters and pixels (roughly 30 to 60 characters, about 560 px before truncation, and Google truncates by pixels not characters), front-loading the keyword, brand placement, why Google rewrites titles and how to reduce it, title vs H1, before/after examples for different page types.

posts.working_title: Meta Descriptions That Get Clicks: Length, Examples, Mistakes
posts.angle: Not a ranking factor but affects click-through; length guidance (about 70 to 155 characters, no official limit), when Google shows other text instead, writing formula, examples for home, product, blog and local pages, and fixing missing or duplicate ones at scale.

posts.working_title: H1, H2, H3: How to Structure Headings for SEO and Readers
posts.angle: What headings do for users, screen readers and search engines, one clear H1, logical nesting (no skipped levels), headings that answer questions, common CMS mistakes (logo as H1, styling text to look like headings), with an outline example.
posts.avoid: Accessibility is covered in depth later; keep it to the heading angle.

posts.working_title: Image SEO: Alt Text, File Size, and Dimensions Done Right
posts.angle: Writing useful alt text (good vs bad examples, decorative images get empty alt), descriptive file names, modern formats (WebP/AVIF), compression, width and height attributes to prevent layout shift, lazy loading below the fold (not the hero image), image sitemaps briefly.

posts.working_title: Structured Data for Beginners: Schema Markup That Earns Rich Results
posts.angle: What structured data is, JSON-LD vs microdata, which types are worth it for small sites (Organization, Article, Product, LocalBusiness, BreadcrumbList; Google stopped showing FAQ rich results in May 2026), how a JSON-LD block is put together, validating with the Rich Results Test and Schema Markup Validator, common errors (markup that does not match visible content).

posts.working_title: Core Web Vitals Explained in Plain English (LCP, INP, CLS)
posts.angle: Hub for performance. What LCP, INP and CLS measure with the official 'good' thresholds (LCP 2.5 s, INP 200 ms, CLS 0.1 at the 75th percentile), field vs lab data, where to check them (Search Console, PageSpeed Insights), the most common fixes for each, and how much they really matter for ranking (part of page experience, not a substitute for relevance).

posts.working_title: JavaScript SEO: When Rendering Hides Your Content From Google
posts.angle: How Google crawls, renders and indexes JS pages, what goes wrong (content or links only after JS, JS changing title/canonical/robots, links without href, blocked resources), SSR/SSG vs CSR in plain English, and how to compare raw vs rendered HTML.

posts.working_title: Mobile-First Indexing: A Checklist for Small Business Sites
posts.angle: What mobile-first indexing means (Google uses the mobile version for indexing and ranking), parity of content, links, structured data and metadata between mobile and desktop, viewport tag, tap targets, font size, intrusive interstitials, and testing.

posts.working_title: Accessibility and SEO: Where They Overlap and Why It Matters
posts.angle: Where accessibility and SEO overlap (alt text, headings, descriptive link text, lang attribute, captions, semantic HTML, contrast for usability), what WCAG is in plain English, automated testing (axe-core) vs manual testing with a keyboard and screen reader, and why automated tools catch only part of the issues.
posts.avoid: Never claim accessibility is a direct ranking factor.

posts.working_title: E-E-A-T in Practice: How to Show Experience on Every Page
posts.angle: What E-E-A-T is (from the Search Quality Rater Guidelines; not a single direct ranking factor), with practical on-page signals: real author bios and author pages, first-hand evidence (photos, screenshots, test results), citing sources, about and contact pages, updating dates honestly, and YMYL topics.

posts.working_title: How to Show Up in Google AI Overviews and AI Search
posts.angle: Grounded only in what Google has publicly said: AI features rely on the same SEO fundamentals, a page must be indexed and eligible to be shown with a snippet, no special markup or AI text files are required. Practical steps: answer questions clearly near the top, structure with headings and lists, keep facts verifiable, structured data that matches visible content, earn mentions. Mention llms.txt as an emerging, unofficial convention that Google does not use. Hedge anything uncertain.
posts.avoid: No invented statistics about AI traffic or click-through.

posts.working_title: Broken Link Building: A Step-by-Step Outreach Process
posts.angle: The full process: pick a niche, find resource pages and dead outbound links by crawling them, check what the dead page used to cover (Wayback Machine), create or match a replacement, write a short non-spammy outreach email (template), follow up once, track results. Ethics and avoiding spam.

posts.working_title: Local SEO Basics: Google Business Profile, Citations, and Reviews
posts.angle: How local results work (relevance, distance, prominence, per Google), setting up and optimizing a Google Business Profile, NAP consistency and citations, earning and responding to reviews within Google policy (no review gating or incentives), local landing pages, LocalBusiness structured data.
